subject: Plain-language snippets for DPA/subprocessor & cross-border section - procurement ask
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@acmeapps.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA / subprocessors wording for procurement review

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Our procurement and security teams have one small ask before we move to redlines: can you provide two short, plain-language blurbs that we can paste into our internal vendor summary? They want one sentence that explains how Redwood uses subprocessors (what they are and why you use them) and one sentence about cross-border transfers and safeguards.

Attached is our standard DPA questionnaire for reference (Acme_DPA_Questions_0421.pdf). Ideally these blurbs are concise (one line each) and match the language you plan to publish in the console/help center.

Appreciate it — procurement is looking to close this week.

—Sam
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Apps Inc.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Questions_0421.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acmeapps.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors wording for procurement review

Hi Sam —

Thanks, attaching two short options below. I looped in Kimberly for Console copy and Laura for the one-line sales-friendly summary in case you want that variation. I also attached a draft snippets file (console-snippets-v1.md) for your team to paste into their vendor sheet.

Option A (explicit):
- Subprocessors: "We engage vetted subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring, and analytics vendors) to operate and maintain the service; subcontractors are contractually bound to handle customer data only as instructed and under equivalent security controls."
- Cross-border transfers: "Data may be processed in data centers or cloud regions outside your country; we use standard contractual safeguards and technical controls to protect data during international transfers."

Option B (concise):
- Subprocessors: "We use trusted subprocessors to run and secure the service; they act only on our instructions and under contract."
- Cross-border transfers: "Your data may be processed globally; contractual and technical safeguards are in place."

Which tone works for procurement — explicit or concise? If you want, Kimberly can tighten the console microcopy to fit the UI length limit and Laura can produce a single-sentence version for sales one-pagers.

Best,
Priya
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console-snippets-v1.md (text, 3KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors wording for procurement review

Thanks Priya — I like Option B for the console (short and scannable). Proposed console-ready lines below with character targets noted:

- Subprocessors (UI, ~120 chars): "We use trusted subprocessors (e.g., cloud infra, monitoring) who act only on our instructions and follow our security controls."
- Cross-border transfers (UI, ~110 chars): "Data may be processed in other countries; we protect transfers using contractual safeguards and strong technical controls."

For the public privacy policy page, I'd keep Option A (explicit) so legal/regulatory readers have the detail. Vanessa — can you verify the subprocessor examples are consistent with our current catalog? Markus — flag if the phrasing conflicts with the new SCC language we rolled out last month.

Quick note to Sam (copied below): if procurement needs a short cert list (SOC 2, ISO/PCI if relevant) we can add that line too.

-Kim
Principal Writer, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors wording for procurement review

Sam —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this. Procurement indicated they prefer the concise console wording (Kim's Option B) for their vendor summary, and they asked for one additional line confirming certifications. Final suggested package below that you can paste into your vendor sheet:

1) Subprocessors (concise): "We use trusted subprocessors to operate and secure the service; they act only on our instructions and are contractually required to follow our security controls."
2) Cross-border transfers (concise): "Data may be processed in other countries; we protect transfers with standard contractual safeguards and technical and organizational measures."
3) Certifications (one-line): "We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 assessments; additional certifications available on request."

I've published the approved console snippets and a short FAQ draft here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Acme-DPA-console-snippets-v2 (comments enabled). Please confirm if that matches what procurement needs and whether you'd like us to add the subprocessor list export or the SOC report access steps.

If it's good, we can proceed to generate the DPA redline and upload the requested evidence into the secure share.

Thanks — look forward to closing this out this week.

—Priya
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
